nodes.kim.text.t: "A wanderer. Everyone here's a wanderer till somebody's hen goes missing. You've a roof at the tavern and work on the board, and keep your questions under your shirt. If you make trouble, I don't answer for you, but you don't answer for me either, so we're square."

nodes.odrzucil.text.t: Wawrzyn blinks as if someone had thrown sand in his eyes. "You refused an order? Then you're either a hero or a gallows bird, and it's best not to sit next to either. But nobody round here loves imperial orders, so I won't give you up. This once."

nodes.p1.options.[p1a].text.t: Nobody. The road just brought me here.

nodes.p1.options.[p1b].text.t: The School of the Blade told me to report in.

nodes.p1.text.t: Wawrzyn puts the chit down upside down and looks at you like a new tax. "A roof and some peace, you won't find those here. But first: who sent you? Nobody comes to Głuszec of his own free will."

nodes.p2.options.[p2b].text.t: From the Ford. I don't remember the rest.

nodes.p2.text.t: "The road brought you, the school sent you, sure. Everyone's got an excuse, hardly anyone's got papers. And where are you coming from? Don't say nowhere, 'cause Nowhere's a hamlet with no name, and we've none of those round here."

nodes.p3.text.t: The reeve leans in and lowers his voice. "And the Imperials? They're not after you, by any chance? 'Cause if they are, you'll get no roof from me, and if they aren't, you will, but it's five groats for me not asking."

nodes.pielgrzym_znikl.text.t: Wawrzyn raises his eyebrows so high they nearly vanish under his cap. "You ran him off? On your own? No stick and no witnesses? I hope you didn't do anything I'll have to not see later. But never mind. Two groats from the reeve for peace on the road."

nodes.potwierdz.text.t: "A room for three groats? Course. At Grumble's that's near enough an honour: if the fleas pass you over, you're a walking curse. Here's ten groats for your trouble, and remember, you never laid eyes on me."

nodes.powitanie.options.[kim].text.t: A wanderer. Looking for work and a roof.

nodes.powitanie.options.[nocleg_raport]..t: I've already got a bed at the tavern.

nodes.powitanie.options.[odrzucil].text.t: I refused an imperial order and stayed here.

nodes.powitanie.options.[pielgrzym_znikl.t: The false pilgrim won't be back.

nodes.powitanie.options.[pytania].text.t: Reeve, I'm looking for a roof and some peace.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q4_start].text.t: I heard someone's squealing to the Imperials.

nodes.powitanie.text.t: Wawrzyn the reeve sits behind a table buried in chits he can't read, pretending to read them. He sizes you up from boots to cap. "And who are you? And what for? And for how long? And who'll vouch for you if anything happens?"

nodes.przyjety.text.t: "So be it. You're in, only I don't know who you are and I don't want to. You've a room at the tavern, work on the board, and in the forest past the village there's poachers doing honest work for a change. Keep to those paths and I'll keep an eye on you." Wawrzyn picks up a chit upside down again.

nodes.q4_koniec.text.t: Wawrzyn listens with the face of a man who's had it all worked out for ages and was only waiting for someone to confirm it. "The false pilgrim. The one who hangs about the road with a wineskin and not a scrap of piety in him. The Imperials pay him for names. Good to know. What I do with him is my business, and you never told me a thing. And one more thing: the digger's been complaining that the stones on an old grave glow at night. Don't go there, unless you've a good reason and not much sense." The reeve waves you off as if shooing a fly.

nodes.q4_start.text.t: Wawrzyn puts down his chit, which happens once a year, and glances at the door in case anyone's listening. "Someone in Głuszec is telling the Imperials who comes through here. Not you, you look like the sort who wouldn't even give himself up. Find out who, but quietly. The wise woman sees who visits whom, and the smith hears what folk say over the iron. Start with them."

nodes.wies.text.t: "Twenty hearths, thirty dogs and one graveyard, the biggest hereabouts. Folk here would sooner die than move away, and nobody knows why. The nearest proper town is Beckby, a day's walk from here, and there's an imperial garrison in it, so anyone with sense keeps away."
